name: advanced heart failure overview
title: Advanced (stage D) heart failure, flagged by I NEED HELP: refer to an advanced heart failure centre; a patient who wants advanced therapy and is advanced enough gets a transplant if there is no contraindication or a ventricular assist device as destination therapy if there is; inotropes are a bridge or palliation; palliative care should start early

root.title: COLD despite therapy: is it ADVANCED heart failure (HF), and which option FITS?
lines: I NEED HELP: Inotropes · New York Heart Association (NYHA) III–IV or high B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP)
End-organ dysfunction · ejection fraction (EF) < 20% · Defibrillator shocks · ≥ 2 HF Hospitalizations in 12 months
Edema or escalating diuretics · Low systolic BP < 90 · Prognostic drugs cut back
→ refer to an advanced HF centre: being referred is NOT being listed

groups.title: WANTS advanced therapy: is it ADVANCED enough?
lines: severe symptoms + cardiopulmonary exercise testing + invasive hemodynamics
not advanced enough → keep up medical therapy (see the HEART FAILURE chart)

tiers.title: Any CONTRAINDICATION to transplant?
lines: • major comorbidity: cancer in 5 years, lung, kidney or liver disease

head: h
Heart transplant
orthotopic: donor heart in place of the recipient's
who: Wants it + advanced enough + NO contraindication
few patients qualify: donors are scarce
tx: bridge with a VAD or inotropes

head: h
Ventricular assist device (VAD)
a pump: ventricle → arterial circulation
who: • not a transplant candidate, but a VAD candidate
• or a BRIDGE to transplant or a decision
tx: driveline out to a controller + battery

head: h
Inotropes
dobutamine, milrinone, dopamine
tx: its negative inotropy no longer helps

head: h
Palliative care
NO therapy cures HF, not even transplant
who: the HF course is unpredictable, so it is often too late
watch: longer life is possible, not promised
